plan: This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with 3 bidders and payment at the second-highest bid. This is a Vickrey auction variant. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy, as it maximizes your utility regardless of what other bidders do. Bidding below your value risks losing a profitable item, while bidding above risks winning an item for more than it's worth.

My goal is to maximize profit. Since this is a single-round game and values are drawn independently, past rounds are irrelevant beyond understanding the game mechanics. This is a second-price auction. A common strategy in second-price auctions is to bid your true value. This is a dominant strategy, meaning it's optimal regardless of what other bidders do. Bidding my value of $22 ensures I win if and only if my value is higher than the second-highest bid, maximizing my expected profit.

I will use a conservative bidding strategy to maximize profit. Since I only have one round, I need to be careful. I will bid slightly above the expected second-highest bid, assuming other bidders will bid close to their values. Given my value of $13, I will bid a bit lower than my value to ensure a positive profit margin if I win, but high enough to be competitive. I'll aim for a bid that gives me a reasonable chance to win while guaranteeing a positive profit.
